learning_outcomes.text: Having theoretical and practical knowledge in the fields of Industrial Relations, Social Policy, Human Resources, and Labor and Social Security Law at national and international levels, and being able to use them in the work environment.
Mastering the basic legislation related to Industrial Relations, and being able to apply and interpret them in practical situations.
Valuing social justice and having a consciousness of social justice.

Having written and oral communication proficiency, being able to express theoretical and practical knowledge related to the field accurately and effectively, conveying information and thoughts in an understandable way, interpreting, critiquing, and possessing high persuasive power.

Being able to think critically, reason to identify the weak and strong points of alternative solutions, evaluations, and approaches to problems, obtain and analyze information from different sources, and also exercise initiative.

Having numerical and statistical research skills and thinking ability, predicting the outcomes of decisions made in line with these, making accurate forecasts; considering causal relationships, having an analytical mindset, and developing a strategic approach.
Being prone to teamwork, possessing leadership qualities, and having the competence to communicate with experts in other fields.
Having knowledge in a foreign language, including word meaning, composition rules, and grammar, and being able to use these qualities in oral and written communication.
Having basic computer usage knowledge; being informed about information systems used in human resources and labor relations, and gaining the skill to use these software.
Being aware of societal, scientific, and professional ethical values.

syllabus_topics: Concept of Occupational Disease and its Historical Development / Introduction to Occupational Diseases
Effects of Working Environment Temperature on Health
Occupational Diseases Caused by Chemical Substances
Occupational Musculoskeletal System Diseases and Ergonomics
Occupational Diseases Caused by Physical Effects (Radiation, Noise, Vibration, etc.)
Principles and Methods of Protection Against Occupational Diseases
Occupational Diseases in the World and Turkey (Occupational Diseases in Developed and Developing Countries)
Identification, Notification, and Provided Aids for Occupational Diseases in Turkish Law
institution: Düzce University — Elektrik-Elektronik Mühendisliği (Electrical-Electronics Engineering), Normal Öğretim
